skill.name: privy
skill.description: Guides developers through Privy authentication, embedded wallet setup, access policies, blockchain transactions, and API integration across supported client and server SDKs.
skill.summary: Plan and review secure Privy authentication and wallet integrations.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: All 31 external-command alerts are Markdown formatting or API identifiers, not executable shell behavior. All nine URL alerts are official Privy references or placeholder API examples and do not perform automatic requests. The wallet transaction method is confirmed as critical, and the curl example can expose an app secret-derived credential.

remediation.issue: The server-side transaction workflow can move cryptocurrency.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before signing or sending. Show network, asset, amount, destination, policy result, and fees. Add limits, allowlists, and idempotency.

remediation.issue: The curl example places an app secret-derived credential in a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Load credentials from protected secret storage. Warn that shell history, process listings, terminal logs, and shared transcripts can expose literal authorization headers.

- **Webhook verification required:** Always verify webhook signatures before trusting the payload. U

- **Missing app client ID:** If deploying across multiple domains, configure app clients in the Dash

content.value_statement: Wallet authentication and transaction flows require careful SDK, policy, and credential choices. This skill guides Privy setup, wallet creation, transaction handling, and webhook verification.
actual_capabilities: Compares embedded and external wallets for different onboarding needs.
Outlines Privy setup for React, Node.js, and REST integrations.
Guides authentication methods, user linking, and wallet creation.
Explains owners, signers, policies, and approval workflows.
Describes Ethereum and Solana transaction endpoints, chain identifiers, and value units.
Provides checks for secrets, webhooks, idempotency, retries, and error handling.
limitations: Does not execute Privy API requests or blockchain transactions by itself.
Does not replace current Privy documentation or verify SDK behavior.
Does not validate deployed code, policy enforcement, or network configuration.
Does not provide legal, custody, compliance, tax, or financial advice.

use_cases.title: Launch embedded wallet onboarding
use_cases.description: Plan a React onboarding flow that combines Privy authentication with embedded wallet creation and ready-state handling.

use_cases.title: Build a server-managed wallet service
use_cases.description: Design a backend wallet service with secure credentials, owners, policies, idempotency, and webhook verification.

use_cases.title: Review treasury transaction controls
use_cases.description: Review approval rules, chain identifiers, value units, policy limits, and monitoring before a treasury workflow reaches production.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a wallet model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare embedded and external wallets for [application]. Users are [audience], and requirements include [authentication, custody, and user experience]. Recommend one model with clear tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new wallet-enabled application.

prompt_templates.title: Create an integration plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Privy setup plan for a [React or Node.js] application. Include configuration, credential storage, ready-state handling, login methods, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design wallet controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Privy wallet policy for [workflow]. Define owners, signers, allowed actions, limits, approval rules, and test cases. Require explicit human approval for transfers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a transaction workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Privy transaction flow: [description]. Identify authorization, chain ID, units, idempotency, webhook, retry, and secret-handling risks. Do not execute any transaction.

output_examples.input: Should a consumer application use embedded or external wallets?
output_examples.output: Use embedded wallets when users need simple onboarding and do not already have wallets. Offer external wallet linking for users who bring existing balances.

output_examples.input: Create a production checklist for a server-managed wallet service.
output_examples.output: Keep the app secret on the server and initialize one backend client. Add owner assignment, restrictive policies, idempotency, verified webhooks, and retry handling.

output_examples.input: Review a server-side Ethereum transfer flow for production readiness.
output_examples.output: Confirm the wallet ID, CAIP-2 chain, recipient, value units, and policy result. Require explicit approval and prevent duplicate submission with an idempotency key.

best_practices: Keep app secrets, signing credentials, and webhook secrets in server-side secret storage. Never expose them to clients or logs.
Use least-privilege owners, signers, policies, and limits. Test allowed and denied actions before production.
Verify webhook signatures and use idempotency keys. Apply bounded backoff for rate limits and record transaction outcomes.
anti_patterns: Do not place real app secrets in source code, browser bundles, command history, or shared transcripts.
Do not send wallet transactions without explicit approval, destination review, network review, and amount validation.
Do not confuse wallet addresses with Privy wallet IDs or mix human-readable asset amounts with base units.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It provides decision guidance, setup patterns, workflows, and review checks for Privy authentication and wallet integrations.

faq.question: Does this skill execute transactions?
faq.answer: No. It supplies planning and review guidance. Any API call or blockchain transaction must be implemented and approved by the user.

faq.question: Which platforms and chains are covered?
faq.answer: It covers client and server SDK patterns, with detailed Ethereum and Solana examples. It also identifies other chains supported by Privy.

faq.question: Do I need a Privy account?
faq.answer: A Privy account is required for an actual integration. You need an application ID, secure server credentials, and configured login methods.

faq.question: How should I protect Privy credentials?
faq.answer: Store app secrets and webhook secrets in protected server-side storage. Keep them out of client code, logs, shell history, and shared transcripts.

faq.question: Can this skill choose my custody or compliance model?
faq.answer: No. It explains technical options, but legal, custody, compliance, tax, and financial decisions require qualified professional review.
